newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers eagerly await rains for sugar beet crop.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers eagerly await rains for sugar beet crop.

text.p: Rainfall is eagerly awaited across Britain's sugar beet growing areas if the 1997/98 crop is to avoid losing the advantage of early sowings, beet experts said on Friday.

Ground drillings were 100 percent complete by April 5, ahead of last year and before the end of British Sugar's recommended drilling period, as farmers took advantage of mild spring weather to sow early.
British Sugar said the crop was holding up well despite the dry conditions.
"This is not really causing us any great problem. The overall picture is that the seed went into very good beds which have moisture in them," said a company spokesman.
"Obviously if there's any instance of seedbeds which have been a bit overworked with a loss of moisture, then they'll need some rain. It's dry but the crop is coping with it," he said.
Beet growers have reported dry conditions in East Anglia and Lincolnshire, two of Britain's major crop areas. Problems of patchy emergence and weed growth have been cited in the latter region.
High daytime temperatures have prevented the application of herbicide to control the weeds.
But the National Farmers Union (NFU) was more sceptical and said the lack of rain could cancel out the advantage of the early sowings.
"We've got a good head start but we may have lost all of that with the lack of rain," a NFU official said.
"It's been one of those years where it's been favourable to get it (beet) in early but looking forward, it's not good. I guess there will be problems with emergence," she added.
Growth of weeds would stunt beet growth so it was important for the seedlings to get a good start.
Another potential problem caused by the higher temperatures would be an increased risk of aphids, which can feed as soon as the beet leaf emerges, leading to the presence of virus yellows, she said.
Independent weather forecaster WSC said on Friday western Europe could expect mostly sunny to partly cloudy weather on Saturday.
The short-term outlook through to Tuesday was for fair and cool weather with no widespread rains expected and temperatures below normal, it added.

"I should imagine that, given a good quantity of rain, it will mean it will shoot up with good sunlight and temperatures -- but it will depend on those seedlings being able to germinate properly," the NFU official said.
"If they can't then we have a problem."
